previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, GERD, and anxiety presented with five days of persistent epigastric discomfort radiating to the throat, accompanied by bothersome belching. The symptoms began after she stopped taking Prilosec due to financial constraints and consumed a large, greasy meal with beer. In the ED, her cardiac workup—including ECG and troponin levels—was unremarkable, and her pain resolved with a GI cocktail. She was admitted for further evaluation and management. During her brief hospitalization, her symptoms were attributed to gastroesophageal reflux disease, and her Prilosec dose was increased to 40 mg daily with insurance coverage confirmed. Her cardiac medications were continued unchanged, and she remained stable. She was discharged home with instructions to follow up with her primary care provider in two to three weeks and to return if concerning symptoms developed.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital because you had pain in your 
stomach that you described as similar to the pain that you had 
prior to your cardiac bypass operation.  For this, you had 
electrical tracings of your heart and blood tests that checked 
if these symptoms were coming from your heart.  You also had a 
stress test to make sure that this did not reproduce your 
symptoms.  The results of these tests showed that it was highly 
unlikely that your heart was causing these symptoms; it is more 
likely that this was being caused by dyspepsia, which is pain 
that originates from your stomach.  This may also be being 
worsened by the stress that you are feeling at home at the 
moment.

For this, you were started on a medication that stops acid 
production in your stomach called pantoprazole.  

You were also found to be hypertensive while in the hospital.  
For this reason, your lisinopril was increased from 5mg to 10mg

Please take all medications as prescribed, and keep all of your 
follow up appointments.
